report_unavailable_tool:web

I can’t quote the California statute or verify your checkout flow against the current law because I don’t have web access and I’m not allowed to rely on or reproduce time‑sensitive statutory text from memory. That means I also can’t produce the required citations right now.

What I can do now (without citing): 1) tell you what I need to review to determine compliance, and 2) give a short checklist of the kinds of items California automatic‑renewal rules typically focus on so you can self‑check or paste your checkout flow/statute text for a targeted analysis.

What I need from you to analyze compliance
- The exact statutory text or a link to the current statute you want me to quote (paste the text here).  
- Or a detailed description / screenshots of your checkout and post‑purchase screens and the cancellation mechanism (wording, placement, pre‑checked boxes, links, confirmation message, retention of proof, etc.).

Checklist of items to gather/check (common legal focal points for automatic‑renewal / negative‑option rules)
- Clear, conspicuous disclosure of the automatic renewal/continuous subscription before purchase (cost, billing frequency, renewal terms).  
- An affirmative consent mechanism (not merely a pre‑checked box) for recurring charges.  
- A clear description of the cancellation method and an easy-to-follow cancellation mechanism (and whether the law requires it to be as easy as enrollment, or requires online cancellation).  
- An acknowledgement sent at or immediately after purchase that repeats the key terms and tells the consumer how to cancel (and whether that acknowledgement must include a cancellation link).  
- Statement of any free trial terms (duration, what triggers charges) and how to cancel during the trial.  
- Requirements for retention of proof (e.g., keeping a record of the consumer’s acceptance/consent).  
- Any specific permitted or prohibited billing practices (e.g., billing prior to renewal, third‑party billing).  
- Any notice timing requirements prior to renewal (e.g., advance notice before charging for a renewal term).  
- Whether the statute applies differently to in‑person, online, or telephonic enrollments, and whether different disclosures/cancellation methods are required.  
- Whether there are special rules for certain products/services (e.g., memberships, subscriptions, digital goods).

How I can help if you supply either:  
- If you paste the statute text, I will quote it precisely and compare each requirement to your checkout flow.  
- If you paste screenshots or a precise description of the checkout flow, I will map each relevant statutory element to your flow and say which elements appear compliant or missing.

Where to verify the statute yourself (so you can paste authoritative text)
- Look up the automatic‑renewal statute on California’s official legislative site (California Legislative Information) or consult a current annotated code via an official or commercial legal research source, and paste the exact statutory language here.

I cannot complete the requested quote or compliance determination until you provide the statute text or give me the checkout details (or until web access is available).
